title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-13
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude Professional v9.11 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: An excellent Charlie Miller sound‑board capture of a 1968 concert that shines with a soaring Dark Star, an epic Eleven, and a fiery Other One→Cryptical.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean, well‑balanced sound‑board source (the Charllie Miller version) that presents the band in top form. Reviewers rave about the Dark Star, The Eleven (with standout vocals from Jerry, Phil and a surprising Weir contribution), and the Other One→Cryptical sequence, while noting a weaker New Potato/Drums segue and a second‑set that doesn’t quite match the first set’s brilliance.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviewers gave 4–5 stars, consistently praising the musical performance and noting only minor recording or set‑list quirks; thus the combined show (70%) and recording (30%) score is very high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Charllie Miller sound‑board version praised as good quality, crisp and balanced; no significant dropouts or muffiness reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is viewed as stronger; second set has an abrupt New Potato‑to‑drums splice and feels less cohesive, ending with a calm feedback/space outro.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Top‑notch guitar tone on Dark Star and Death Don't Have No Mercy; feeds off the band’s energy.
band_member_comments.Phil: Fabulous bass work and vocal contribution to The Eleven; part of the tight group interplay.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal part on The Eleven is highlighted as a surprise strength, despite earlier doubts about his role.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers are described as fabulous overall, though the dedicated Drums segment was considered less interesting.
